#127731. A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1152 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has made an unexpected discovery in our own solar system.
  • Sources indicate that the achievement is particularly remarkable given that Euclid was built to capture detailed images of distant galaxies rather than track rapidly moving objects such as comets.
  • Mikko Pöntinen, a PhD student at the University of Helsinki, made the discovery with the Solar System Objects Science Working Group of the Euclid Consortium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has made an unexpected discovery in our own solar system. Images captured between September 16 and 24, 2026, revealed a previously unknown comet, the first discovered by the mission.

Sources indicate that the achievement is particularly remarkable given that Euclid was built to capture detailed images of distant galaxies rather than track rapidly moving objects such as comets. The speed with which researchers identified and confirmed the discovery demonstrates that Euclid can detect newly introduced comets while they are still relatively far from the Sun. This capability could eventually help identify a target for ESA's upcoming Comet Interceptor mission.

A Mysterious Streak Reveals a Upcoming Comet.

Mikko Pöntinen, a PhD student at the University of Helsinki, made the discovery with the Solar System Objects Science Working Group of the Euclid Consortium. Pöntinen developed specialized software to detect and track small solar system objects appearing in the telescope's images.

Industry observers note that "I was excited to see my software flag a 'streak' smeared across several images -- the result of a fast-moving object. By predicting its position I could identify it in other images, in total finding it in five image sets. Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas.".

Industry observers note that the object appeared in a region of the sky known as the 'Euclid Deep Field North'. Over several days, the telescope captured it in five separate fields of view, taking between two and four exposures of each field for a total of 16 exposures.

After searching catalogs of known asteroids and comets without finding a match, Pöntinen submitted the observations to the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center (MPC) as a potential new comet. The report enabled astronomers using telescopes on Earth to carry out additional observations. On October 8, the MPC officially confirmed the discovery. The comet has been designated C/2026 S1 (Euclid).

A Comet on an Extraordinary Orbit.

Sources indicate that the newly discovered comet is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers (about 800 million miles) from Earth. That distance is comparable to the distance from the Sun to a point somewhere between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn.

However, the comet is traveling well outside the relatively flat plane in which the planets orbit the Sun. It is presently positioned almost directly above the Sun, following a sweeping path over the solar system that will take thousands of years to complete.

In a recent development, the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center (MPC) serves as the central international hub for observations of asteroids and comets. It gathers data from observers around the world to verify discoveries, determine orbital paths, and assign official designations. As additional observations become available, astronomers will be able to calculate the orbital period of C/2026 S1 (Euclid) more precisely.

Why Euclid Rarely Discovers Latest Comets.

Industry observers note that although Euclid has spotted comets before, all of them had already been discovered. Several aspects of the telescope's design and observing strategy make finding previously unknown objects within our solar system especially difficult.

Euclid intentionally avoids the region of the sky surrounding the plane of the solar system, where large numbers of asteroids and comets can be found. Dust concentrated in this region produces unwanted light that could interfere with the telescope's sensitive observations of the distant universe.

Industry observers note that the spacecraft also follows a 'step-and-stare' observing strategy, typically imaging each section of the sky only once. This means researchers cannot readily direct Euclid back toward a newly detected comet to gather more information about it.

Industry observers note that identifying objects within our solar system is nevertheless an important part of Euclid's scientific work. Researchers must account for everything appearing in its images so that unrelated features, including comet trails and unwanted light, can be removed without compromising the accuracy of its galaxy measurements.

"Very few comets are expected to be discovered by Euclid so it was a happy coincidence that the combination of the comet's orbit and Euclid's scanning over those days captured the object in multiple images," says Bruno Altieri, Euclid Archive Scientist, and part of the discovery team.

Preparing for a Future Comet Encounter.

Euclid's unexpected discovery also provides valuable experience for scientists working on ESA's future Comet Interceptor mission. Although the newly identified comet is not an appropriate destination for the spacecraft, the successful detection and rapid notification process demonstrates how the two missions could work together to identify potential targets.

Sources indicate that "While this particular comet is not a suitable candidate for Comet Interceptor, the process of discovery and alert gives us a real test case for how our two mission teams will coordinate in the future. And we are of course happy to have discovered a previously unknown comet for the Solar System community to follow-up on," adds Valeria Pettorino, Euclid Project Scientist.

Ancient Remnants of the Solar System.

Recent findings suggest that comets are ancient bodies composed of ice and dust that remain from the formation of our solar system approximately 4.6 billion years ago. Most originate in the distant Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud, regions located beyond the orbits of the outer planets (interstellar comets come from other solar systems).

Industry observers note that as a comet approaches the Sun, increasing temperatures cause its ice to turn directly into gas. Escaping gas and dust form a glowing, fuzzy cloud known as a 'coma,' as well as an extended tail.

In a recent development, because comets native to our solar system have remained relatively unchanged since their formation, they preserve valuable evidence of the materials and environmental conditions that existed when the planets were taking shape. Studying these ancient objects may also help scientists understand the origins of Earth's water and the chemical building blocks of life.

Euclid's Hunt for Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

In a recent development, the primary goal of the Euclid mission is to uncover how dark matter and dark energy influence the visible universe. During its six-year survey, the space telescope will examine the shapes and movements of billions of galaxies at distances reaching up to 10 billion light-years.

According to recent reports, the comet discovery was reported on behalf of the Solar System Objects Science Working Group of the Euclid Consortium by M. Pöntinen, A. A. Nucita, A. Franco, M. Granvik, B. Altieri, S. Kruk, B. Y. Irureta-Goyena and B. Carry.

Materials provided by European Space Agency. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Tech Report: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Both Russian and international media refer to the satellite communications network Rassvet (Dawn) as the "Russian Starlink," a satellite internet service operated by the US firm SpaceX.
  • Rassvet, which was developed by the Russian aerospace manufacturer Bureau 1440, operates in low Earth orbit.
  • Recent findings suggest that interest in the system surged after the Russian military lost access to Starlink terminals, which until then had ensured communications and internet access in the battle zone in Ukraine.On the front, for example, Starlink helps drone pilots and commanders receive images from drones equipped with cameras.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Both Russian and international media refer to the satellite communications network Rassvet (Dawn) as the "Russian Starlink," a satellite internet service operated by the US firm SpaceX.

Rassvet, which was developed by the Russian aerospace manufacturer Bureau 1440, operates in low Earth orbit.

Recent findings suggest that interest in the system surged after the Russian military lost access to Starlink terminals, which until then had ensured communications and internet access in the battle zone in Ukraine.On the front, for example, Starlink helps drone pilots and commanders receive images from drones equipped with cameras. Military personnel also communicate together thanks to Starlink.

Though Russia does not fall within Starlink's area of coverage, the Russian military managed to acquire "illegal" terminals through third countries and was thus using the same system as the Ukrainian army.

In early 2026, SpaceX, in coordination with the Ukrainian Defense Ministry, introduced a "whitelist," which registered all devices on Ukrainian territory authorized to operate on the Starlink network. Any terminals being used by Russian forces were subsequently deactivated, and reports of serious communication problems on the front then began to appear in Russian social media channels.

In May, the US news channel Bloomberg reported that the Ukrainian army had recaptured about 400 square kilometers (ca. 155 square miles) of Ukrainian territory since Russian forces lost access to Starlink.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Two first launches of serial Rassvet satellites took place in March and July 2026.

According to information from Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) published by the Reuters news agency in early November, Russia has started using Rassvet for military communications over Ukraine and to carry out attacks.

The system is reportedly being used to improve strike accuracy, expand capabilities of reconnaissance drones and to strengthen resilience against electronic warfare.

HUR spokesperson Andriy Yusov also told Reuters that "the constellation is currently insufficient to provide uninterrupted coverage of Ukrainian territory.".

Georgiy Trishkin, a rocket analyst and operator of Telegram channel Tekhassky Vestnik (The Texas Herald), told DW that Russia aims to have a functioning "sovereign" alternative to Starlink — consisting of 292 satellites in orbit — running by the end of 2027.

According to Serhii Beskrestnov, aka Flash, an advisor to the Ukrainian president, the main danger posed by the Rassvet system is that it could allow the Russian army to control drones over Ukrainian territory.

He also pointed out on the platform Facebook that the Ukrainian military cannot use Starlink to control drones over Russian territory, since the US service does not work there.

Recent findings suggest that inspired by the Starlink model, the Russian military also wants to be able to equip drones with terminals, which will enable connectivity in more remote parts of Ukrainian territory. Bureau 1440 unveiled some initial models last month, but according to Trishkin, the similarities between Rassvet and Starlink stop at the "basic features and concept.".

"When it comes to details, these are completely different projects. No one can currently match SpaceX's technological edge — and especially its lead in production technology," he said, pointing out that while the Starlink constellation comprised over 10,000 satellites, Rassvet would not have more than 300 in its first phase.

He added that Bureau 1440 would struggle to make enough of the kits used on the ground. While SpaceX can manufacture about 15,000 per day, this would be a "remarkable achievement even over the course of a year" for the Russian tech giant.

He also mentioned that the terminals produced by Bureau 1440 were much more expensive than those by Starlink as they relied "on foreign components.".

Industry observers note that "Right now, no one can beat SpaceX in terms of price, volume and quality of service," Trishkin mentioned. "The next step for the manufacturer is mobile satellite services, where it's making very rapid progress. Will Bureau 1440 be able to respond? Unlikely for the time being.".

SpaceX's Starlink was primarily designed as a civilian service, while Starshield is more for government and military sectors.

According to DW sources, Rassvet was likely designed to support battlefield communications and thus does not currently require as many satellites as Starlink.

Ukrainian military expert Oleh Starikov said that if Rassvet continues to develop as it has then it could fulfil the mission put to it by the Russian military. He added that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk was developing a system that would work around the world, whereas Bureau 1440's satellites sufficed for Russian military purposes.

But he also underlined the massive expansion of Russia's satellite network generally, which — on January 1, 2022, before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine — comprised 102 satellites according to Dmitry Rogozin, who at the time was general director of the Russian space agency Roscosmos.

In September of this year, Rogozin's successor Dmitry Bakanov stated that the number almost quadrupled.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that recent restrictions to Starlink services in Ukraine have brought the matter to the fore again. In mid-November, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy noted that Starshield had been throttled in Ukraine.

"Unfortunately, our units have been recording significant disruptions to Starshield's operations over the territory of Ukraine for several days now — along the entire front line and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine," he remarked, adding that the restrictions occurred at speeds of 161 km/h and higher.

Restrictions on the use of Starlink were first put in place on October 14 and then lifted, according to US President Donald Trump, on October 23.

When asked by DW whether the Ukrainian military could gain access to Rassvet, Trishkin said it was "only a matter of time" before terminals fell "into foreign hands and are subsequently examined.".

This article was originally published in Russian.

#127726. Tech Report: Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1298 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.
  • In a recent development, the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.

In a recent development, the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S. has shifted in recent years. In 2010, about 60% of clothing was predominantly made from cotton. Now, that total is around 45%, while predominantly synthetic fabrics such as polyester and nylon comprise the majority of imports.

According to recent reports, apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index. Since 2020, they have soared to record highs.

In a recent development, it's starting to change habits for consumers who are paying more for food, gas, rent and other staples. As shoppers shell out more for clothes, they're increasingly making sure the garments are worth the cost.

Consulting firm AlixPartners' 2026 Consumer Sentiment Index, which surveyed more than 9,000 shoppers, found that consumers are scrutinizing labels more closely and rejecting cheap materials sold at a premium.

"If it's not a natural material, a retailer brand who passes it off as it is, they're really becoming very low on consumers' minds," noted Sonia Lapinsky, head of fashion at AlixPartners.

In a recent development, fast fashion brands like Forever 21 and H&M exploded in popularity during the early 2000s and 2010s, bringing trendy clothing to shelves quickly at low prices. Then came ultra-fast fashion, with brands like Shein and Fashion Nova pumping out fresh garments at even quicker speeds and lower price points — made possible in part through the use of inexpensive, synthetic fabrics.

In a recent development, "We got to a point where the pendulum just swung too far in that direction. And we've actually begun to see a reversal," said U.S. Bancorp BTIG consumer analyst Janine Stichter. "Quality matters a lot more ... over the last three or four years than it has in the previous 10 or 20.".

But quality, which shoppers often tie directly to material, can come at a higher cost.

Recent findings suggest that the average unit price of apparel imported to the U.S. between January and August was $2.64 per square meter for garments that were predominantly synthetic fiber, like polyester and nylon, compared with $3.67 for items that were largely cotton, according to data from the U.S. Commerce Department's Office of Textiles and Apparel.

When comparing those 2026 figures to 2010, synthetic fiber apparel import costs have climbed around 11%, while cotton apparel costs have risen 21%.

"If you're appealing to a more value-sensitive customer, you either reduce the quality, or you negotiate with suppliers to try to share some of the cost or you maybe absorb the cost … and perhaps hope to crank a higher volume of product to make up for it," said Bernstein Research senior retail analyst Aneesha Sherman.

Though polyester is cheaper, experts point out that's not necessarily a bad thing. It can help clothing hold its shape and wick away sweat.

Sherman believes the athleisure boom is a primary factor in the shift toward polyester. She said that from 2015 to 2025, sports apparel was growing at a 4.9% rate in the U.S., versus 2.6% for all apparel and footwear, according to Euromonitor data.

"There probably is some quality trade down as well happening there," Sherman remarked. "But I think both these trends are conflated.".

Industry observers note that nonetheless, backlash to synthetic materials is growing. Gen Z has even repurposed the word "polyester" as an insult to mean generally low-quality or fake.

Concerns have also grown about the environment and human health surrounding petroleum-based clothing, as more research indicates microplastics can leach from polyester clothing when washed.

It's led consumers to reexamine what materials are in their clothing.

Sources indicate that apparel prices have risen coming out of the pandemic, as demand outpaced supply and allowed companies to raise prices, said BTIG's Stichter. Tariffs and the Iran war followed, raising costs for businesses — and prices for consumers.

Petroleum is the basis of many synthetic fibers, and oil prices have skyrocketed since the start of the Iran war.

The same factors that helped drive up prices of clothing — Covid, tariffs and war — also affected clothing quality.

"Companies had to move around their supply chains in the post-Covid period," stated Stichter. "They had to find ways to take costs out, and sometimes that meant using less expensive fabrics.".

Those factors compounded a more-than-decade-long shift away from manufacturing in China.

Sheng Lu, a fashion and apparel studies professor at the University of Delaware, whose research focuses on the economics of the global textile industry, said China's established history with clothing production means it has higher-skilled workers, state-of-the-art-equipment and better material management compared with emerging manufacturing destinations such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.

According to recent reports, "They mostly serve the value market and the mass market. And I think the reason why they're not ready to make higher-quality luxury and premium products really reflects the kind of skill sets you can expect when you source from these countries," noted Lu.

AlixPartners' Lapinsky remarked these countries that manufacture at a lower cost sometimes have to still ship the raw materials from China, which can extend the timeline to make clothing. That means taking earlier bets on trends and then discounting if products don't sell well.

"If you have to mark down that product because the consumer doesn't want it as much, your net margin might actually be worse than if you were to just invest in quality in the first place," noted BTIG's Stichter.

And as material costs rise for synthetic fibers, Stichter also remarked she believes it could further influence companies to use more natural fabrics moving forward.

Companies prioritizing quality are winning in this environment.

Ralph Lauren's stock is up around 85% over the past two years. Around 90% of its apparel is primarily made of cotton, leather, wool, viscose, cashmere or silk, according to its 2026 sustainability report. In its fiscal 2026, the company noted it sold more products at full price and reduced markdowns.

Meanwhile, direct-to-consumer clothing brand Quince, which centers its brand identity around natural materials, reached a $10 billion valuation this year.

In a recent development, the brand jumped 16 spots to No. 3 for best resale value in online consignment retailer ThredUp's 2025 report. Organic cotton retailer Pact jumped 20 spots on that list to No. 8, illustrating the potential role materials are playing in brand recognition.

Alternatively, the 2026 AlixPartners report, which ranks sentiment for brands in different retail categories, found shoppers are viewing some fast fashion brands less favorably. Both Shein and Zara dropped three spots — to fifth and seventh place, respectively — in terms of sentiment in the young adult specialty category.

Shein passed higher tariff costs onto shoppers in 2025 and then blamed a sales slowdown on those higher prices. The ultra-fast fashion retailer saw its year-over-year share of U.S. apparel, accessories and footwear card spending decrease in the fourth quarter of 2025 and first two quarters of 2026, according to Consumer Edge.

Shein did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

It has been revealed that though Zara fell in AlixPartners' Consumer Sentiment Index, it has continued to grow sales and profits year over year. Even so, Lapinsky remarked worsening consumer views are something to watch, even if the tech giant is doing well.

It has been revealed that "What we found over the years with this consumer sentiment index is that sometimes it will be a bit of a leading indicator of what's to come," said AlixPartners' Lapinsky. "I'm not saying that this is going to be true for Zara, but I think that's one thing that we'll be watching as we look in the upcoming quarters and into 2027.".

X implements parental controls for teen customers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk's social network X just got a upcoming feature it never had under previous ownership.
  • That would be parental controls for teen users, to be exact.
  • Sources indicate that these features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require new followers to be approved by the parent or guardian.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk's social network X just got a upcoming feature it never had under previous ownership.

That would be parental controls for teen users, to be exact. In a new post from the official Safety account on X, the firm declared it has implemented parental controls for users aged 13 to 17. The way it works is that an account run by a parent or guardian establishes a supervisory link to the account run by a teen, which gives the parent or guardian access to a bunch of monitoring and safety features the site didn't have before.

Sources indicate that these features include the ability to monitor usage and set daily limits for the teen, as well as the option to require new followers to be approved by the parent or guardian. Recommendations on the For You feed can be limited to accounts the teen already follows, while parents can mute specific words, control who can send direct messages, and see who the teens have chatted with in DMs without seeing the messages themselves.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Industry observers note that as X noted, this only starts when both parties in the equation consent to it, so a teen cannot have their account limited against their will. Theoretically, anyway. A parent account can supervise as many as five teen accounts, but a teen account can only be linked to one parent account.

This is interesting because it's an acknowledgment by X that some teenagers do use the platform, but even in the Safety account's post, the company is clear that X is "not designed for or promoted to children." Indeed, one could argue that teen users should stay far away from a service that has become home to hate speech, widespread misinformation, and a Grok AI chatbot that has gotten up to plenty of unsavory business since it was introduced.

But if teens are going to use X, at least these features exist now.

Topics Apps & Software X/Twitter Elon Musk.

Alex Perry is a tech reporter at Mashable who primarily covers video games and consumer tech. Alex has spent most of the last decade reviewing games, smartphones, headphones, and laptops, and he doesn’t strategy on stopping anytime soon. He is also a Pisces, a cat lover, and a Kansas City sports fan. Alex can be found on Bluesky at yelix.bsky.social.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The 78-year-old businessman and U.S.
  • Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".

He should know. The 78-year-old businessman and U.S. Navy veteran helped with his own succession planning and recommended to GM's board in 2013 that Barra replace him as CEO. She has held the top job since Jan. 15, 2014.

Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.

Sources indicate that "It's going to be very, very dynamic," Akerson told CNBC during a phone interview. "It's going to be a big change.".

Akerson declined to discuss potential internal candidates such as GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, CFO Paul Jacobson or President Mark Reuss, but he noted the eventual successor needs to be dynamic and, if from the outside, "adaptable.".

It has been revealed that his comments to CNBC follow a Wall Street Journal report on Tuesday that GM is working with an executive search firm to identify possible outside candidates to succeed Barra, in addition to internal prospects. GM declined to comment on the report or Barra's succession.

Akerson, who came to GM as an outsider from The Carlyle Group in 2010, stated selecting an outside candidate might be risky if there are already executives within the organization who have similar leadership and technical expertise.

"Is there anybody in the organization that has that background that you know better day to day over a period of time? You may be taking a risk by bringing in an outsider," he stated.

The prospect of an outsider leading GM would be unusual in the auto industry, where major automakers have generally promoted internal CEO candidates, apart from periods of exceptional disruption such as the Great Recession.

Stellantis, BMW, Toyota Motor, Nissan Motor and Hyundai Motor have all appointed internal executives to their CEO positions in recent years.

Barra has said several times that her successor and her longevity in the role would be determined by the board.

A notable influence is likely Hewlett Packard veteran Patricia Russo, GM's longest-serving board member who has been on the board since 2009 and leads its CEO succession planning as independent lead director.

GM's CEO succession planning is done "at least annually," according to the firm's yearly proxy filing. That process includes Barra providing the board "with recommendations for, and evaluations of, potential CEO successors and discusses developmental aims for these successors," according to the filing.

That is followed by board members engaging "with CEO candidates and senior management talent at Board and committee meetings and other forums to enable directors to personally assess candidates.".

When Akerson was preparing to retire, Barra was among a pool of four candidates — two longtime GM employees and two relative newcomers — who were finalists for CEO in 2013, he said.

Akerson stated he put the finalists through an extended evaluation, asking how they viewed GM's strengths and weaknesses, how they would organize the firm, and their willingness to work together, potentially with other CEO candidates who didn't get the job.

In a recent development, akerson said the final decision to appoint Barra was done at a day-and-a-half-long board meeting in Washington. The candidate field was narrowed to Barra and former GM executive Dan Ammann, an ex-Wall Street banker who was GM's CFO before leaving the automaker's Cruise unit, reportedly over a disagreement in strategy with Barra, in 2021.

Sources indicate that "Mary's very deserving of all the accolades she's received," Akerson said. "She's done a terrific job.".

Barra has been leading the automaker for nearly 13 years, which makes her the longest-serving CEO of the automaker since Alfred Sloan retired after a 23-year career as CEO in 1946.

Akerson mentioned he believes that, like he did, Barra will have major influence in picking her successor. He described that dynamic as integral to continuing her legacy leading the automaker.

In a recent development, "This is vital. I think if she doesn't pick the right person, in four or five years from now and things are back in the trough, that will tarnish her history. But I think she'll pick the right one," he said.

Deep beneath Australia, hidden caves could unlock the secrets of alien worlds

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1048 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, stretching over 200,000 square kilometers across southern Australia, the vast, flat plains of the Nullarbor mark one of the world’s largest regions of limestone.
  • Ultimately, this led to the familiar dry landscape of today, which has acted as a significant barrier for plants, animals, and poorly adapted colonial Victorian-era explorers who described it as “the sort of place one gets into in bad dreams”.
  • In contrast, the Mirning People of the Nullarbor and Great Australian Bight have lived for tens of thousands of years on this southern margin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, stretching over 200,000 square kilometers across southern Australia, the vast, flat plains of the Nullarbor mark one of the world’s largest regions of limestone. It formed when an ancient shallow sea retreated some 14 million years ago.

Ultimately, this led to the familiar dry landscape of today, which has acted as a significant barrier for plants, animals, and poorly adapted colonial Victorian-era explorers who described it as “the sort of place one gets into in bad dreams”.

In contrast, the Mirning People of the Nullarbor and Great Australian Bight have lived for tens of thousands of years on this southern margin. They have watched the landscapes change and sea levels fall and rise with the build-up and collapse of the last ice age about 20,000 years ago.

Industry observers note that to an untrained eye the Nullarbor Plain appears deceptively simple and featureless. However, beneath the immense plain lies a remarkable, largely hidden underground world.

It has been revealed that over millions of years, water has eaten away at the limestone and created complex cave networks that can extend for kilometers underground. Sadly, the caves remain poorly understood, partly because they’re only really known and accessible where they breach the surface.

According to recent reports, our newly introduced study, published in Communications Earth & Environment, reveals a new way to track these cave systems even when they are deeply buried. Our work helps explain the formation of previously mysterious, shallow trench features on the Nullarbor. It also provides a new way to identify hidden caves elsewhere – even beyond our own planet.

Scattered across the Nullarbor are tell-tale signs of its vulnerability to being dissolved – small cave openings and shallow depressions.

But there are also structures of previously unknown origin and significance: long (up to 20 km), shallow (a few meters) trenches that trend roughly north-south. They’re almost invisible from the ground, but we can clearly see them in modern digital landscape models.

Industry observers note that these shallow trenches look somewhat like flat-bottomed valleys, but they were not carved by rivers. They begin and end abruptly and are not connected to existing rivers or drainage networks that extend into the upland areas around the Nullarbor.

They also lack typical river branching patterns and the sediments within them don’t show any evidence of being deposited from flowing water.

To understand how these strange structures formed, we combined several investigative techniques.

Industry observers note that first, we mapped the trenches using drone and aerial photography, as well as detailed satellite-based digital landscape models. Then the layers of soil and rock were measured in boreholes and caves.

Finally, we used specialized geophysical techniques to “see” inside the Earth, somewhat similar to the way an X-ray enables us to see our internal body structures from the outside.

The work demonstrated that the shallow surface trenches sit above deep zones of broken rock, and in places line up with known cave systems and sinkholes.

In a recent development, this means the trenches are mere muted surface expressions of deeply buried cave systems. These systems are slowly, over millions of years, “collapsing upwards” through the overlying rock layers to reach the surface.

Industry observers note that the results of this work will change how scientists interpret cave landscapes globally. It shows that to explain the surface structures we see, we must look deeper than we might think.

Understanding where voids may exist underground can be crucial for planning both surface (buildings, roads) and subsurface (tunnels, sewers) engineering works, mitigating geological hazards, and accessing and protecting groundwater resources.

Pockmarked karst landscapes (where rocks are dissolved by water, resulting in caves and sinkholes) represent 15% of the ice-free Earth’s surface and supply water to 10–25% of the global population.

It has been revealed that more fundamentally, caves are important scientific archives. Because caves are sheltered from surface weathering and erosion processes, they can preserve snapshots of ancient environments and ecosystems that would otherwise be lost to time.

Furthermore, they may host an array of strange and vulnerable life-forms that have evolved and adapted in isolation. These are some of the least studied organisms on Earth.

In a recent development, to learn more, we must first locate the cave structures. And the results of our study could be very vital in this regard.

The implications of this new work even extend beyond our own planet. Because caves offer a stable environment and shelter from damaging space radiation, they provide promising exploration sites for life on other planets.

Mapping of planetary surfaces within our Solar System has identified numerous potential caves, including some thought to be related to karst on Mars.

Recent findings suggest that the Nullarbor’s dry, stable surface is an excellent analogue to help locate the subtle surface fingerprints of hidden cave systems on planets that now lack a dynamic water-cycle – such as Mars. Even if the caves are barren of life, they could be attractive bases for future human explorers.

How many other apparently simple landscapes around the world or on other planets are concealing large cave systems underneath? We don’t yet know, but the trenches we studied are unlikely to be unique. Similar subtle landforms are likely to have been overlooked elsewhere, too.

Sometimes the most remarkable discoveries are waiting in understated but plain view, in landscapes we think we already understand.

According to recent reports, the authors would like to acknowledge Matthias Leopold from The University of Western Australia; Rok Ciglič, Mateja Ferk, Jure Tičar, Matija Zorn and Matej Jelovčan from the Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts (ZRC SAZU); John A. Webb from La Trobe University; Uroš Stepišnik, Matej Dolenec, Primož Miklavc, Tomislav Popit and Andrej Šmuc from the University of Ljubljana; and Jian-xin Zhao from The University of Queensland.

#127717. Tech Report: Thuma Dupes: Japanese Joinery Bed Frames That Stack Up (2026)

📅 10 Sep 2025 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2411 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Thuma Dupes: Japanese Joinery Bed Frames That Stack Up (2026)

📅 10 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that japanese joinery bed frames are bolt-free beds made from notched wood pieces that slide and click together to make a stable frame.
  • Thuma is the leading brand in this space, and we love its product lineup—several members of the WIRED Reviews team have tested Thuma beds, and all rave about them.
  • Recent findings suggest that japanese joinery is a traditional carpentry method that uses only wooden components.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silk & Snow (queen, with solid headboard).

Industry observers note that japanese joinery bed frames are bolt-free beds made from notched wood pieces that slide and click together to make a stable frame. Think Jenga, but with really nice, sleek wooden furniture. The advantages are many, starting with easy assembly that takes just a few minutes and requires no tools.

Thuma is the leading brand in this space, and we love its product lineup—several members of the WIRED Reviews team have tested Thuma beds, and all rave about them. However, they’re not cheap. A Thuma bed frame starts at $895 for a twin frame with no headboard, and the king-sized Thuma signature bed our testers loved costs $2,500.

Recent findings suggest that japanese joinery is a traditional carpentry method that uses only wooden components. Instead of nailing boards together, each piece of wood is carved so it snugly fits into openings carved into neighboring pieces—the “joints,” if you will. The tension and strong hold of the interconnected pieces create structural integrity.

In a recent development, it’s a pretty easy way to channel your inner Bob the Builder, and the finished bed frame looks stunning in its simplicity. However, we are always on the lookout for products at the intersection of high quality and low price—curious to see if any contenders could give Thuma a run for its money—so we researched and tested, and these are our findings.

Be sure also to check out our guides on the best mattresses we’ve tested, as well as the best pillows and bedsheets. You’ll need something to put on your latest frame, after all!

Updated November 2026: We’ve added two new bed frames to this guide and ensured accuracy throughout.

DreamCloud (queen, with bamboo headboard).

In a recent development, I’m a longtime fan of DreamCloud mattresses, so it came as no surprise that the brand’s Japanese joinery bed frame is excellent. Like the mattress, this frame has numerous thoughtful details that stood out immediately.

DreamCloud made setup seamless. Each piece is labeled, and when it comes time to put it all together, take a gander at the endpoints of the long pieces. If you look closely at the joints where they intersect at the ends, you will see holes drilled into the top and bottom pieces. Small rods attach to the boards and fit into them, serving as a secondary mechanism to ensure stability. I find this impressive because the beams stack neatly into the grooves carved into the ends. In a word, it’s crisp. It’s a tiny detail, but the frame stayed virtually silent when I put a mattress on it or moved around in my sleep. I didn’t notice any shaking, either.

Recent findings suggest that another excellent feature is the frame’s center stability beam (crucial for preventing long-term sagging), which slides in last. This lets you avoid nesting it before closing the frame, unlike some other Japanese joinery models from different brands. It’s far more convenient.

Sources indicate that lining up the slats is the most challenging part of the process; you have to make sure everything is aligned perfectly. To help the process go smoothly, you’ll find wooden rods—similar to those on the ends of the boards—in the center of the bed, where you insert the slatted frames. They’re about the width of a pencil. Pop those slats in, unroll, Velcro to keep in place, and go.

You don’t need a headboard with this frame, but DreamCloud provided one for testing. Two square openings are located inside the top beam of the frame, right where your head would be. The headboard slides into these internal slots, which hold the end pieces and keep it upright. Foam block stickers are included to be attached last, so your wall doesn’t get scuffed up. All that, and still no tools necessary. Down to the details, people! And this detail you don’t want to skip—it’s around $449 for a queen. The headboard costs $299 extra, but even with that, it’s still far cheaper than luxury alternatives. You’ll also have two stain options: natural or a very pretty walnut.

That stated, you’ll have to consider how many sleepers will use this frame and the weight of the mattress you’ll place on it. When I was testing new mattresses every week, two of the frame’s center support legs split right down the middle. Make sure you don’t screw them on too tightly, as I suspect the tension is what made the wood look like I had been chopping it with a small axe. Regardless, I was shocked to see this happen, and it is another notch on Thuma’s belt for heightened durability. —Julia Forbes.

The Bamboo Bed Frame by DreamCloud ranges from $299 for a twin to $549 for a California king (frame only).

Silk & Snow (queen, with solid headboard).

Recent findings suggest that silk & Snow is another brand that I hold in high regard. Every time I’ve tested a mattress from the brand, it consistently packs quality for the price. This platform bed frame was no exception. There are two options: natural rubberwood and acacia wood. I opted for the latter, which is a medium-brown color. I thought that the stain was stunning, with a richness akin to a lovely latte. However, I really appreciate that they offer options not just in wood stain color, but also in the actual hardwood itself.

In a recent development, this frame arrived in four separate boxes. I liked this approach because it protected the wood stain’s integrity during shipping. Every other frame in this guide was packed into one box—not unlike a mattress-in-a-box, but heavier and longer. I actually preferred this route, as every box was also labeled for easy setup.

Like the DreamCloud frame, Silk & Snow’s doesn’t require tools or hardware to set up—it’s made entirely of wood. One thing I learned the hard way: Make sure the center beam is within the frame perimeter before fully closing it off. Then place the slats into the internal notches on the side rails, and it’s ready for a mattress. I had no challenges with noise, shaking, or feeling unstable. It supported a mattress just fine, and I am still truly enamored with how the wood stain looked amidst my studio’s decor.

However, I do a lot of testing, so I’m constantly setting up and taking down mattresses, frames, and bedding. This is where having two people will be crucial, as I decided to do it all by myself for the sake of time, to the detriment of the frame. The frame got badly scratched up around the slatted portions where the corners of the boards stack together, due to my awkward solo assembly motions. I doubt you’ll be doing this as much as I do, but it was still a bit disappointing to see. Despite this, it’s worth recommending because I loved how it looked and performed. —Julia Forbes.

The Silk & Snow Wooden Platform bed frame ranges from $550 for a twin to $900 for a king (frame only).

The Avocado City Bed Frame is a minimalist wood (blonde or walnut) platform frame with a completely tool-free Japanese-joinery assembly process. The same natural, nontoxic, and sustainable materials practices that guide the firm’s mattresses are at play here as well.

The City Bed is regularly $1,299 for a queen, and it is the most affordable of Avocado’s bed options (though you have to factor in a shipping fee). It’s made from very nice, solid wood (I tested the walnut version). There’s an optional headboard that I did not test. The bed itself is attractive, fairly subtle, and unobtrusive. In fact, if your duvet is reasonably large, you may not even see much of the bedframe.

According to recent reports, the frame fits together using interlocking joints with metal reinforcements. In my testing, it’s been solid and sturdy, with no squeaking or any signs of weak joints. It is a tight fit at times, especially at the four corners, and I had to tap it with a soft mallet to get it fully flush (which sort of defeats the no-tool promise, but you probably could have done the same with a copy of Infinite Jest or something equally solid). —Scott Gilbertson.

The Avocado City bed frame ranges from $750 for a twin to $1,499 for a California king (frame only).

Industry observers note that the Birch frame was the most basic of the Thuma dupes I tested. I was really excited about this one because the wood is sourced from the land of the pines, otherwise known as my home state of North Carolina. Poplar is a durable hardwood, and southern yellow pine is one of the harder pine woods. (I can attest to this because, for an eighth-grade science project, I tested the durability of regional woods.) The manufacturing partner is a certified member of the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC). The legs are made of a completely different wood, Appalachian maple. It also uses a soy-based resin to remain completely formaldehyde-free.

In a recent development, it arrived in two boxes, and setup was quick and easy—the step-by-step instructions were the most thorough of the bunch. With written descriptions and pictures, it’s hard to mess this up. Plus, you don’t need any tools to get this frame up and running. The outer boards were polished to maintain the gorgeous hue of the pine wood. However, be cautious when handling the inner slatted-board sections, as this wood is not finished. I got a small splinter and was not a happy camper. Next, I set up the bed and slept on it for a week—the standard amount of time I test mattresses. The first few days, this thing creaked and moaned like crazy. It didn’t feel stable, and I was shaken if I moved even slightly. By the end of the week, it seemed to fall into place and settle, so I no longer noticed the noise or motion.

It has been revealed that I don’t want to discount this as a possible option, though, because the wood quality was what I wanted it to be, and so was the overall price. If you’re looking for a cheaper option for a guest room, upgrading your teen’s room, or furnishing a first apartment on a budget, this could work well for you. —Julia Forbes.

The Birch Madison bed frame ranges from $749 for a twin to $978 for a California king.

Nectar Sleep (queen, frame only).

Nectar Sleep (queen, with bamboo headboard).

It has been revealed that I had never set up or slept on a Japanese joinery-style bed frame before testing this model from Nectar, and now I’m a true believer. The frame is made from bamboo, and assembly took just about 20 minutes with no tools required.

It has been revealed that putting it together was super simple: the four feet had cut-out notches where the frame slid into place, and you just needed to push down to make the pieces lock together—it’s essentially like putting together a giant set of Lincoln Logs. After sliding the footboard into the feet’s notches, you finish both sides the same way by pushing down into the notches. The middle section is springy and has a floating foot to adjust for the bed’s pressure, so no cumbersome box spring is needed. The slats are connected with Velcro and just need to be unspooled and adhered to the sides. I opted for a headboard that slides in from above and stays in place because of the cutouts on the head portion of the frame below.

Sources indicate that I’m physically disabled, so putting together furniture with tools and nails or screws is nearly impossible. I recommend that anyone who’s in a similar position check out a Japanese-style bed frame, as it’s lightweight, requires no additional tools, and requires very little physical strength. Plus, this frame comes in two colors, has optional headboard attachments, a 60-night home trial, a two-year warranty, and free shipping. —Molly Higgins.

The Nectar Bamboo bed frame ranges from $299 for a twin to $549 for a California king (frame only).

Here’s the thing: Thuma is still a Japanese joinery bed frame. Therefore, I’d be remiss not to include it on this list. While I can vouch that the options above are credible dupes, many of my teammates feel nothing beats the original in this case.

In a recent development, thuma’s Classic Bed Frame is made from upcycled, sturdy rubberwood that comes in four finishes: walnut, natural, espresso, and gray. You can also choose different headboard variations, including all-wood, a pillow board (Italian wool and foam), or a hybrid of the two. The design’s not only beautiful, but it’s also backed by certifications such as UL GreenGuard Gold and CertiPur-US (if you opt for the pillow board).

WIRED Gear Editor Julian Chokkattu has had his Thuma frame for several years, and he notes it takes next to no time to set up. He also loves that it doesn’t creak or slide—just a strong sense of security while sleeping on it.

The Thuma Classic bed frame ranges from $895 for a twin to $1,495 for a California king (frame only).

Just like with the best mattresses we regularly test, each frame required a week of testing (not including naps) to evaluate night-over-night performance. This also allowed time for the frames to settle into place and perform alongside the bed each was paired with.

How Do I Set Up a Japanese Joinery Bed Frame?

Recent findings suggest that your bed frame should come with installation instructions, whether it features Japanese joinery construction or not. In the same vein, I recommend having someone assist you with the setup. As mentioned in our Silk & Snow review, this helps mitigate the risk of bumping and scratching your fresh furniture.

Are These Bed Frames Better Than Thuma’s?

We wouldn’t say better, just different. Each brand offers its own approach to creating a bed frame that adheres to the Japanese joinery method. This could include the type of wood used, the stains offered, the types of headboards you can pair it with, where it was manufactured, and, of course, the price.

Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (929 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that first there was an attack on a Russian cargo vessel, the Sparta II, off the Finnish coast, then on the Russian corvette Merkury and a dry cargo vessel that was allegedly carrying weapons off the coast of Libya.
  • Intelligence agencies have long warned that Russia was preparing some form of provocation along NATO's eastern flank.
  • What are the risks of Russia's war in Ukraine escalating further and drawing in other regions?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that first there was an attack on a Russian cargo vessel, the Sparta II, off the Finnish coast, then on the Russian corvette Merkury and a dry cargo vessel that was allegedly carrying weapons off the coast of Libya. These spectacular Ukrainian operations in regions far from the Ukrainian capital Kyiv have caused a stir. They came shortly after several suspected Russian missiles crashed in Poland, not far from where an international military exercise was underway.

Intelligence agencies have long warned that Russia was preparing some form of provocation along NATO's eastern flank.

What are the risks of Russia's war in Ukraine escalating further and drawing in other regions?

It is no secret that Russia has long since expanded its operations beyond Ukraine: With military provocation, hybrid operations and acts of sabotage, Moscow has attempted to put pressure on the countries that openly support Ukraine.

And Ukraine has also targeted Russia's military and economy beyond its borders.

Industry observers note that since the summer, attacks by both Russia and Ukraine have increased in the Black Sea. Not only have Russian and Ukrainian cargo ships been targeted, but also vessels from other countries, particularly Turkey.

Furthermore, in the past few years, Ukraine has managed to deal significant blows to Russia, deep within Russian territory, thanks to aerial and maritime drones. It has targeted military airfields and other strategic targets such as oil refineries, including one in Omsk, Siberia, as well as military vessels in the eastern Black Sea.

In a recent development, russia has access only to a very narrow strip of the Baltic Sea coast, which is flanked by Finland and Estonia. Even ahead of the attack on the Sparta II, Ukraine had struck in the area multiple times, targeting oil terminals in the region around St. Petersburg, in Ust-Luga and Primorsk.

Russia uses the Baltic Sea to transport supplies to its Kaliningrad exclave and to export oil and other goods to the rest of the world, with the help of its "shadow fleet.".

Ukrainian special forces are also said to have carried out operations against Russian military facilities in Syria, well before the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024. They are also reported to have lent support to local Tuareg fighters in Mali who were able to inflict heavy losses on the Malian army and allied Russian mercenaries.

Kyiv is thus attempting to harm Russia's military and economy worldwide, even if in military terms this does not help Ukraine directly.

The Russian corvette that was sunk was part of Russia's Black Sea Fleet but because of Turkey's blockade of the Bosporus and the Dardanelles, it would not have been allowed to return to the Black Sea. Instead, it was escorting Russian cargo ships in the Mediterranean. Primarily, the attacks send a political message: Russian ships can no longer feel safe — anywhere in the world.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "We are not speaking about random shadow vessels which simply transport oil above the price cap and as a result bring revenues for the Russian treasury," security expert Elisabeth Braw from the Atlantic Council told DW. Sparta II was suspected of carrying military equipment, which Moscow denies.

According to recent reports, "Ukraine is showing that it knows exactly, and secondly that it's able to hit them wherever and whatever waters they are in," Braw continued. "And this is something I don't think Ukraine has been able to do at the beginning of the war.".

Officially, Kyiv's goal is to disrupt Russian logistics and supply routes, but military experts and politicians also see the attacks as a clear political signal to Western allies. They suspect that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is sending a clear message of strength with an eye toward possible future peace negotiations.

In a recent development, in an interview on the German news outlet Tagesschau, security expert Joachim Weber from the University of Bonn suggested that Zelenskyy was paying less attention to the US, out of a sense of disappointment. He said that Ukrainian attacks in distant maritime areas were a sign that there was less inhibition and that Ukraine was ready to expand the conflict geographically to increase pressure on Russia, despite the risks.

Recent findings suggest that weber warned that war could become omnipresent if there was an increase in attacks on civilian vessels or ships that were considered suspicious in international waters. He noted that Russia was providing more military escorts for the ships of its shadow fleet. "The likelihood that an accidental exchange of fire between armed forces, coast guards or anyone could occur is rising.".

Braw pointed out that violations of the Law of the Sea were not only rising with regard to the Russia-Ukraine war but also in relation to other conflicts and playing out in "the South China Sea, the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.".

She said about 90% of global trade today was conducted via the oceans and she feared that others might conclude it was not "really to their advantage" to follow the rules of international maritime law.

It has been revealed that she added that they might find it "beneficial in the short term to violate maritime rules" for short-term gains. "That would make the world's oceans significantly less safe for everybody.".

Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.
  • It has been revealed that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it.
  • Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person stated, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

It has been revealed that the balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person stated, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”.

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have remarked.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”.

Industry observers note that gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”.

Industry observers note that the surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

In a recent development, still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

CNN’s Alex Marquardt contributed to this report.

Breaking: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • More than a mile below the surface of the Red Sea, researchers from the University of Miami (UM) Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science discovered rare deep-sea brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, a northern extension of the Red Sea.
  • Recent findings suggest that the discovery was made by Sam Purkis, professor and chair of the UM Department of Marine Geosciences, and his colleagues in collaboration with OceanX.
  • In a recent development, "Until we understand the limits of life on Earth, it will be difficult to determine if alien planets can host any living beings," mentioned Purkis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than a mile below the surface of the Red Sea, researchers from the University of Miami (UM) Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science discovered rare deep-sea brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, a northern extension of the Red Sea. These unusually salty underwater lakes could provide clues to how Earth's oceans formed millions of years ago and help guide the search for life on other planets.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery was made by Sam Purkis, professor and chair of the UM Department of Marine Geosciences, and his colleagues in collaboration with OceanX. The researchers located the pools at a depth of more than one mile (1,770 meters) using a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) deployed from the OceanXplorer, an advanced research vessel equipped to investigate some of the least accessible environments on Earth.

In a recent development, "Until we understand the limits of life on Earth, it will be difficult to determine if alien planets can host any living beings," mentioned Purkis. "Our discovery of a rich community of microbes that survive in extreme environments can help trace the limits of life on Earth and can be applied to the search for life elsewhere in our solar system and beyond.".

Life thrives in extreme underwater lakes.

In a recent development, brine pools rank among the harshest environments on our planet. Their waters contain exceptionally high concentrations of salt, feature unusual chemical conditions, and are completely devoid of oxygen. Despite these seemingly inhospitable conditions, the pools support abundant microbial life. Previous research on microbes inhabiting Red Sea brine pools has even identified biologically active molecules with potential anticancer properties.

The findings, published in Communications Earth & Environment, mark the first documented discovery of brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba. Remarkably, the researchers nearly missed them.

According to recent reports, "We were very lucky," said Purkis. "The discovery came in the last five minutes of the ten-hour ROV dive that we could dedicate to this project.".

Hidden records of ancient tsunamis and earthquakes.

Industry observers note that beyond their biological significance, the pools serve as natural archives of the region's geological history. Situated relatively close to the coastline, their extremely salty waters and absence of oxygen help preserve evidence of tsunamis, flash floods, and earthquakes that occurred in the Gulf of Aqaba thousands of years ago. Regional tectonic activity has produced numerous faults and fractures across the seabed in this part of the gulf.

According to recent reports, earlier in 2022, Purkis and his colleagues uncovered evidence of a 500-year-old underwater landslide that likely generated a substantial tsunami. Understanding the region's history of such events could have important implications for coastal development in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

The study, titled "Discovery of the deep-sea NEOM Brine Pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea," was published on June 27, 2022, in Communications Earth & Environment.

The research team included Sam J. Purkis, Hannah Shernisky, Peter K. Swart, Arash Sharifi, Amanda Oehlert, Gaëlle Duchâtellier, James Klaus, Gregor P. Eberli, Larry Peterson, and Graham Kolodziej from the UM Rosenstiel School; Fabio Marchese and Francesca Benzoni from King Abdullah University of Science and Technology's Red Sea Research Center; Giovanni Chimienti from the University of Bari Aldo Moro in Italy; Andrew Craig and Mattie Rodrigue from OceanX; Jürgen Titschack from MARUM -- Center for Marine Environmental Sciences in Germany; and Ameer Abdulla from NEOM.

NEOM, a firm developing the Saudi Arabian coastline, provided funding for the four-week research expedition aboard the OceanXplorer.

Watch the NEOM OceanX documentary about the discovery: https://youtu.be/bWNftnYDx9c.

Tech Report: Pizza chains are under pressure. GLP-1 use is only one part of the problem

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Big pizza chains are struggling as weaker consumer spending, a wider variety of dining options and the rise of GLP-1 medications weigh on their sales.
  • The pandemic was a boom time for Domino's Pizza, Papa Johns, Little Caesars and Pizza Hut.
  • These days, consumers are watching their discretionary spending but have more delivery and takeout options when they do decide to order, thanks to the accessibility of third-party platforms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Big pizza chains are struggling as weaker consumer spending, a wider variety of dining options and the rise of GLP-1 medications weigh on their sales.

The pandemic was a boom time for Domino's Pizza, Papa Johns, Little Caesars and Pizza Hut. But since dining rooms reopened, the biggest U.S. pizza chains have faced an uphill battle to retain their customers.

These days, consumers are watching their discretionary spending but have more delivery and takeout options when they do decide to order, thanks to the accessibility of third-party platforms. Plus, food quality and the customer experience have become more important to diners who are looking for value when they order from restaurants.

As a result of pizza fatigue and challenges facing the broader restaurant industry, the number of U.S. pizza restaurants has tumbled. Since pizza locations hit a peak of 83,035 nationwide in August 2019, more than 9,600 pizzerias had closed their doors as of July 2026, according to data from Datassential.

Sources indicate that in 2025, sales at U.S. pizza restaurants fell 0.3%, according to Technomic data. Sales at independent pizzerias slipped 0.4%. Chains, which account for about two-thirds of the domestic pizza category sales, saw revenue shrink 0.3%.

Papa Johns reported that North American same-store sales declined 2.5% in 2025. Pizza Hut's U.S. same-store sales fell 5%. Among the three pizza chains that were publicly traded last year, only Domino's posted annual same-store sales growth at its U.S. restaurants, with an increase of 3%.

According to recent reports, it isn't just diners who have lost their appetite for pizza. Since March 2020, Papa Johns stock has lost about two-thirds of its value. Even shares of Domino's, which dominates the category, have seen gains of only about 2% in that time. For comparison, the S&P 500 has climbed about 150% over the same period.

And Yum Brands sold Pizza Hut this year, offloading the laggard of its portfolio to LongRange Capital and Yum China after about two decades of stagnating sales.

"Pizza Hut has been a detractor for YUM ... Going forward, YUM won't be tripped up by pizza category dynamics (discounting, etc.), translating to stronger growth and higher concentration in higher growth industry segments and markets," Wells Fargo analyst Zachary Fadem wrote in a research note in September.

Pizza chains now have significantly more competition for diners' dollars than they did in 2020. Third-party delivery platforms, which grew in popularity during the pandemic, offer a wide variety of cuisines beyond the traditional pizza and Chinese. As a result, Domino's and Papa John's have to compete with other fast-food chains, like McDonald's and Chick-fil-A, for DoorDash and Uber Eats orders.

As pizza has grown more expensive, a pie seems less appealing to budget-conscious diners. The average large cheese pizza is now almost $17, according to the 2026 Pizza Power Report from PMQ Pizza, a trade publication.

Sources indicate that plus, frozen pizza is another convenient option, with a lower price tag. Retail sales of single- and multi-serve frozen pizza rose 2.9% in the 52 weeks ended Nov. 7 compared with the same period in 2022, according to NielsenIQ data.

"When the American consumer is focused on the least expensive eating occasion, the items that are in my pantry, my refrigerator and my freezer win every single time," noted David Portalatin, a food and food service industry advisor for Circana.

Convenience stores like Casey's General Stores have also won over customers with pizza at a low price point.

"We believe that [Casey's] has an advantage over [quick-service restaurants] and dollar stores, which have fewer options to navigate the persistent inflationary environment, while [Casey's] can offset food pressures with margins," Bank of America Securities analyst Sara Senatore wrote in a research note published in June.

She added that geographic overlap of locations suggests that Casey's is stealing share from Pizza Hut.

The biggest pizza chains have also been slow to adapt to shifting consumer attitudes toward nutrition. For example, of the four biggest chains, Papa Johns is the only one to even test a pizza crust with added protein as more diners prioritize it in their diets. And the test was only in one Atlanta restaurant — for a single day.

In a recent development, pizza's nutritional content more broadly is another drag for the category. Its carbohydrate and fat content, from its dough and cheese, respectively, can make it less appealing for consumers on GLP-1 drugs, which have skyrocketed in use over the last several years.

Spending on pizza quick-service restaurants has fallen 22.2% per GLP-1 household after six to eight months using the medications, according to a 2026 survey published by PwC.

To be sure, pizza's recent struggles do not mean an existential crisis for the category. Total pizza servings are down only about 1% this year, Circana's Portalatin stated.

Recent findings suggest that and chains are trying to reverse that downturn in servings. In August, Domino's launched the Domino, a customizable Detroit-style personal pizza to attract solo diners. In November, Papa Johns unveiled a new turnaround plan focusing on improving food consistency and restaurant operations. And Pizza Hut is running a holiday-themed meal deal.

"Pizza's not going anywhere," Portalatin said. "The American consumer loves pizza.".
